topics.name: Vector Multiplication
topics.description: Fundamental operations for multiplying vectors in optics, including dot products yielding scalars and cross products yielding perpendicular vectors.

key_concepts.name: Dot Product
key_concepts.description: Multiplication of two vectors yielding a scalar equal to the product of their magnitudes and the cosine of the angle between them.

key_concepts.name: Cross Product
key_concepts.description: Multiplication of two vectors yielding a third vector perpendicular to both, with magnitude proportional to the sine of the enclosed angle and direction determined by the right-hand rule.

topics.name: Multidimensional Derivatives
topics.description: First-order vector differential operators in Cartesian and curvilinear coordinates, specifically the gradient, divergence, and curl.

key_concepts.name: Gradient
key_concepts.description: A vector derivative of a scalar function representing the direction and rate of fastest spatial change.

key_concepts.name: Divergence
key_concepts.description: A scalar differential operator applied to a vector function, representing the net outward flux per unit volume.

key_concepts.name: Curl
key_concepts.description: A vector differential operator describing the infinitesimal rotation or circulation of a vector field.

topics.name: Laplacian Operator
topics.description: A second-order differential operator defined as the divergence of a gradient, applicable to both scalar and vector fields.

key_concepts.name: Scalar Laplacian
key_concepts.description: The divergence of the gradient of a scalar function, reducing in Cartesian coordinates to the sum of the second partial derivatives.

key_concepts.name: Vector Laplacian
key_concepts.description: A second-order derivative acting on vector fields, given coordinate-independently by the relation ∇²E = ∇(∇·E) - ∇×(∇×E).

topics.name: Vector Integral Theorems
topics.description: Fundamental integral theorems relating volume, surface, and line integrals of vector fields in physical contexts.

key_concepts.name: Divergence Theorem
key_concepts.description: An integral identity stating that the surface integral of a vector field over a closed boundary equals the volume integral of its divergence.

key_concepts.name: Stokes' Theorem
key_concepts.description: An integral identity relating the flux of the curl of a vector field across an open surface to the line integral of the field along the bounding curve.

topics.name: Complex Numbers and Euler's Formula
topics.description: Complex-number representations of sinusoidal wave phenomena and trigonometric identities used to simplify optical calculations.

key_concepts.name: Euler's Formula
key_concepts.description: The mathematical relationship connecting complex exponentials to trigonometric functions: e^(iφ) = cos φ + i sin φ.

key_concepts.name: Trigonometric Identities via Complex Exponentials
key_concepts.description: Derivation and verification of angle addition and Pythagorean identities using complex exponential representations of sine and cosine.

topics.name: Complex Number Fundamentals and Geometry
topics.description: Cartesian and polar representations of complex numbers in the complex plane, quadrant corrections, complex conjugates, and the physical interpretation of complex angles in optics.

key_concepts.name: Polar Representation and Quadrant Adjustment
key_concepts.description: Geometric conversion of a complex number a + ib to polar form rho * exp(i*phi), requiring an adjustment of phi by pi when the real part a is negative.

key_concepts.name: Complex Conjugate and Magnitude
key_concepts.description: Negating the imaginary component to obtain z* = a - ib, used to calculate the magnitude |z| = sqrt(z*z) and extract the real part via (z + z*)/2.

key_concepts.name: Complex Angles in Wave Optics
key_concepts.description: Complex angles and wavevectors that describe exponential growth, absorption, or evanescent waves when light undergoes total internal reflection beyond the critical angle.

topics.name: Complex Wave Representation
topics.description: Representation of real sinusoidal waveforms using complex exponentials, enabling linear mathematical operations prior to extracting the real part.

key_concepts.name: Complex Notation for Cosine Waves
key_concepts.description: Expressing A*cos(alpha + beta) as the real part of A_tilde * exp(i*alpha), where phase is embedded in the complex amplitude factor.

key_concepts.name: Linear Operations on Complex Representations
key_concepts.description: Performing linear operations such as addition, differentiation, and integration on the full complex function and deferring real-part extraction to the end.

topics.name: Linear Algebra for Optical Systems
topics.description: Formulation and solution of systems of linear equations using 2x2 matrices, matrix multiplication, inversion, and determinants.

key_concepts.name: Matrix Representation of Linear Equations
key_concepts.description: Encoding two simultaneous linear equations with two unknowns into a 2x2 matrix multiplying a 2D column vector.

key_concepts.name: 2x2 Matrix Inverse and Determinant
key_concepts.description: Computing the inverse of a 2x2 matrix via its determinant AD - BC to solve for unknown vector elements.

topics.name: Sylvester's Theorem
topics.description: Method for calculating powers of a 2x2 matrix with unit determinant, applied to periodic optical multilayer coatings and ray reflections in laser cavities.

key_concepts.name: Sylvester's Theorem Formulation
key_concepts.description: Evaluating an N-th matrix power for a 2x2 matrix with AD - BC = 1 using trigonometric terms involving theta, where cos(theta) = (A + D)/2.

key_concepts.name: Inductive Proof of Sylvester's Theorem
key_concepts.description: Proving that Sylvester's theorem holds for N+1 given that it holds for N, applying the condition AD - BC = 1.

topics.name: Fourier Series and Analysis
topics.description: Decomposition of complex optical fields into superpositions of harmonic sinusoidal waves and expansion of periodic functions into Fourier series.

key_concepts.name: Fourier Decomposition in Optics
key_concepts.description: Decomposing complex light fields into sinusoidal waves that travel independently through frequency-dependent optical media.

key_concepts.name: Fourier Series Expansion
key_concepts.description: Representing a periodic function of period 2pi/Delta_omega as an infinite summation of sine and cosine terms or complex exponentials.

topics.name: Fourier Integral and Continuous Transform
topics.description: Determination of Fourier expansion coefficients via integration and extending the Fourier series to nonperiodic functions in the infinite period limit.

key_concepts.name: Fourier Coefficient Calculation
key_concepts.description: Determining coefficients c_m by integrating the product of f(t) and exp(i*m*Delta_omega*t) over the fundamental period, leveraging orthogonality.

key_concepts.name: Continuous Fourier Limit for Nonperiodic Waveforms
key_concepts.description: Extending the period to infinity by taking the limit Delta_omega -> 0, allowing nonperiodic waveforms such as short laser pulses to be represented.

topics.name: Fourier Integral and Transforms
topics.description: Formulation of the Fourier integral theorem from calculus summations, defining forward and inverse Fourier transform pairs connecting time and frequency domains.

key_concepts.name: Fourier Integral Theorem
key_concepts.description: The representation of an arbitrary function as a continuous limit of a summation over finely spaced frequency steps.

key_concepts.name: Fourier Transform and Inverse Transform
key_concepts.description: The dual integral transformations converting a time-dependent function into a frequency-dependent function and vice versa, noting convention choices in exponential signs and factors of 2pi.

key_concepts.name: Gaussian Wavepacket Transformation
key_concepts.description: Calculation demonstrating how a Gaussian envelope carrier wave transforms between temporal and spectral domains and recovers its original form.

topics.name: Dirac Delta Function and Parseval's Theorem
topics.description: Mathematical formulation of the Dirac delta function as an integral operator and frequency superposition, and its application in proving Parseval's theorem.

key_concepts.name: Dirac Delta Function
key_concepts.description: An idealized function that is zero everywhere except where its argument is zero, which samples the value of another function within an integral and can be represented as a uniform superposition of frequencies.

key_concepts.name: Parseval's Theorem
key_concepts.description: Theorem equating the integral of the squared magnitude of a function in the time domain to that of its Fourier transform in the frequency domain.

key_concepts.name: Three-Dimensional Delta Function
key_concepts.description: Spatial generalization of the delta function arising from the divergence of the inverse-square vector field (r - r') / |r - r'|^3.

topics.name: Mathematical Integrals and Series for Optics
topics.description: Analytical reference formulas for Gaussian integrals, Bessel function integrals, sinc integrals, and geometric series frequently used in optical calculations.

key_concepts.name: Standard Optics Integrals
key_concepts.description: Definite integrals involving Gaussian profiles, Bessel functions (J0 and J1), and sinc-squared functions used in diffraction and wave calculations.

key_concepts.name: Geometric Series Formulas
key_concepts.description: Finite and infinite series summation formulas for powers of a common ratio r.

topics.name: Vector Calculus Tools and Integral Theorems
topics.description: Vector algebraic operations, differential identities, coordinate system transformations, and integral theorems applied in electromagnetism and optics.

key_concepts.name: Vector Algebraic and Differential Identities
key_concepts.description: Properties including the BAC-CAB rule, orthogonality of cross products, curl of curl, and divergence of cross products.

key_concepts.name: Laplacian in Cylindrical Coordinates
key_concepts.description: The differential form of the Laplacian operator expressed in terms of radial, azimuthal, and longitudinal coordinates.

key_concepts.name: Stokes' and Divergence Theorems
key_concepts.description: Theorems relating surface integrals to line integrals (Stokes') and volume integrals to closed surface flux integrals (divergence theorem).

topics.name: Complex Numbers in Optics
topics.description: Algebraic manipulation of complex numbers, Euler's formula representations, and methods for evaluating products of the real parts of complex wave fields.
subtopics: Products of real parts of harmonic fields

key_concepts.name: Complex Number Conversions and Identities
key_concepts.description: Techniques for converting complex expressions between rectangular and polar forms and expressing trigonometric functions via Euler's formula.

key_concepts.name: Products of Real Parts of Complex Fields
key_concepts.description: Identity for evaluating the product of the real parts of harmonic electric and magnetic fields, resolving into time-averaged and rapid-oscillation components.

topics.name: Foundations and Scope of Optics
topics.description: Overview of topics covered in physics-based physical optics, including wave propagation, boundary effects, polarization, coherence, diffraction, and required mathematical preparation.

key_concepts.name: Core Topics of Physical Optics
key_concepts.description: The study of light in matter, reflection and transmission at interfaces, polarization, dispersion, coherence, imaging, diffraction, and the quantum nature of light.

key_concepts.name: Mathematical Preparation for Optics
key_concepts.description: Prerequisite mastery of differentiation, integration, trigonometry, algebra, complex numbers, vector calculus, and Fourier transforms.

topics.name: Fourier Theory and Convolution
topics.description: Mathematical properties of the Fourier transform, including linearity, scaling, time shifts, and the convolution and autocorrelation theorems.

key_concepts.name: Fourier Transform Operational Properties
key_concepts.description: Basic properties of Fourier transforms including linear superposition, time scaling, and time shifts.

key_concepts.name: Convolution Theorem
key_concepts.description: Theorem stating that the Fourier transform of the convolution of two functions is proportional to the product of their individual Fourier transforms.

key_concepts.name: Autocorrelation Theorem
key_concepts.description: Theorem stating that the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation of a function is proportional to the squared magnitude of its Fourier transform.

topics.name: Overview of Maxwell's Equations
topics.description: Introduction to the four fundamental equations of electricity and magnetism, uniting electromagnetic theory with light.

key_concepts.name: Maxwell's Equations
key_concepts.description: The concise set of four equations (Gauss' Law, Gauss' Law for magnetism, Faraday's Law, and Ampere's Law revised by Maxwell) forming a self-consistent electromagnetic theory.

key_concepts.name: Electromagnetic Nature of Light
key_concepts.description: The realization that light is an electromagnetic wave traveling at the speed of light, establishing Maxwell's equations as the foundation of optics.

topics.name: Gauss' Law for Electric Fields
topics.description: Relationship between electric charge distributions and the resulting electric fields in differential and integral forms.
subtopics: Coulomb's Law and continuous charge distributions

key_concepts.name: Coulomb's Law for Continuous Charge Distributions
key_concepts.description: The electric field produced by continuous distributions of charge throughout a volume.

key_concepts.name: Differential Form of Gauss's Law
key_concepts.description: The divergence of the electric field equals the charge density divided by the permittivity of free space.

key_concepts.name: Integral Form of Gauss's Law
key_concepts.description: The net flux of the electric field through a closed surface is proportional to the total enclosed charge.

topics.name: Gauss' Law for Magnetic Fields
topics.description: The formulation of magnetic fields generated by current distributions and the absence of magnetic monopoles.

key_concepts.name: Biot-Savart Law
key_concepts.description: The law defining the magnetic field produced by a steady current density distributed throughout a volume.

key_concepts.name: Gauss's Law for Magnetism
key_concepts.description: Statement that the divergence of the magnetic field is identically zero, derived from the Biot-Savart law.

topics.name: Faraday's Law of Induction
topics.description: The principle that time-varying magnetic fields induce circulating electric fields.
subtopics: Integral and differential forms of Faraday's Law

key_concepts.name: Electromagnetic Induction
key_concepts.description: A changing magnetic flux through a surface bounded by a closed path induces an electric voltage around that path.

key_concepts.name: Differential Form of Faraday's Law
key_concepts.description: The curl of the electric field is equal to the negative time rate of change of the magnetic field.

topics.name: Ampere's Law
topics.description: The relationship connecting magnetic field curl to electric current density, derived through the inversion of the Biot-Savart Law.
subtopics: Current density and magnetic field curl

key_concepts.name: Inversion of the Biot-Savart Law
key_concepts.description: Mathematical derivation taking the curl of the Biot-Savart integral to isolate the current density.

topics.name: Maxwell's Adjustment to Ampere's Law
topics.description: Generalization of Ampere's law for non-steady-state situations by incorporating the continuity equation and displacement current.
subtopics: Continuity equation for charge and current

key_concepts.name: Steady-State Limitation of Ampere's Law
key_concepts.description: Uncorrected Ampere's law applies only when divergence of J is approximately zero, failing for time-dependent phenomena such as optics.

key_concepts.name: Continuity Equation
key_concepts.description: A statement of charge conservation relating the divergence of current density to the rate of change of charge density (div J = -d rho / dt).

key_concepts.name: Displacement Current
key_concepts.description: A time-varying electric field term added to Ampere's law that acts like a current in producing magnetic fields.

topics.name: Polarization of Materials
topics.description: Decomposition of charge and current densities in media and formulation of Maxwell's equations in terms of the polarization vector.

key_concepts.name: Current Density Decomposition
key_concepts.description: Partitioning of total current density into free currents, magnetic currents, and polarization currents.

key_concepts.name: Polarization Vector and Polarization Current
key_concepts.description: The macroscopic dipole distribution P and the effective current J_p = dP/dt arising from time-varying bound charge movement.

key_concepts.name: Bound Charge Density
key_concepts.description: Local concentration of charge resulting from nonuniform arrangements of dipoles, defined as rho_p = -div P.

key_concepts.name: Maxwell's Equations in Polarized Media
key_concepts.description: Macroscopic Maxwell's equations expressed in electrically neutral, nonmagnetic media using polarization P.

topics.name: The Wave Equation
topics.description: Derivation of the decoupled second-order differential wave equation from Maxwell's equations in media and vacuum.
subtopics: Derivation of the electromagnetic wave equation
Wave propagation in vacuum and the speed of light

key_concepts.name: Derivation of the Wave Equation
key_concepts.description: Deriving decoupled second-order differential equations for electric and magnetic fields using the curl of Faraday's law and vector identities.

key_concepts.name: Source Terms in the Wave Equation
key_concepts.description: Terms on the right-hand side of the material wave equation representing free current dynamics, dipole oscillations, and anisotropy.

key_concepts.name: Vacuum Wave Equation and the Speed of Light
key_concepts.description: Homogeneous wave equation in vacuum yielding shape-preserving propagating waveforms moving at c = 1 / sqrt(eps_0 mu_0).

topics.name: Mathematical Tools
topics.description: Foundational mathematical tools for optics, including vector calculus, complex numbers, linear algebra, and Fourier theory.

key_concepts.name: Vector Calculus in Cartesian Coordinates
key_concepts.description: Representation of spatial position by Cartesian vectors using unit basis vectors, essential for electromagnetic equations.

key_concepts.name: Fourier Theory
key_concepts.description: Mathematical framework of Fourier transforms applied to spectral and pulse analysis in optics.

topics.name: Electromagnetic Phenomena
topics.description: Fundamental laws of electromagnetism including Gauss's, Faraday's, and Ampere's laws, Maxwell's equations, material polarization, and electromagnetic wave equations.

key_concepts.name: Maxwell's Equations
key_concepts.description: Set of four fundamental equations describing electric and magnetic fields, charge, and current distributions.

key_concepts.name: Electromagnetic Wave Equation
key_concepts.description: Wave equations derived from Maxwell's equations describing the propagation of electric and magnetic fields in vacuum at speed c = 1/sqrt(epsilon_0 * mu_0).

key_concepts.name: Measurement of the Speed of Light
key_concepts.description: Determination of light speed through experimental techniques, such as Roemer's observations of Jupiter's moon Io and rotating mirror methods.

topics.name: Plane Waves and Refractive Index
topics.description: Plane wave solutions to the wave equation, complex representation, refractive index, dielectric models, and wave irradiance.
subtopics: Plane Wave Solutions to the Wave Equation
Index of Refraction of a Conductor

key_concepts.name: Plane Wave Solutions
key_concepts.description: Solutions of the wave equation where wavefronts form planar surfaces propagating along a specified wave vector direction.

key_concepts.name: Lorentz Model of Dielectrics
key_concepts.description: Physical model explaining the dispersion and frequency dependence of the refractive index in dielectric media.

topics.name: Reflection and Refraction
topics.description: Behavior of electromagnetic waves at planar boundaries, Fresnel coefficients, reflectance, transmittance, polarization effects, and total internal reflection.

key_concepts.name: Fresnel Coefficients
key_concepts.description: Coefficients characterizing amplitude reflection and transmission for electromagnetic waves at an interface.

key_concepts.name: Brewster's Angle
key_concepts.description: The specific angle of incidence where reflected light is completely polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence.

key_concepts.name: Total Internal Reflection
key_concepts.description: Optical phenomenon occurring when light incident on a boundary at angles beyond the critical angle reflects completely.

topics.name: Multiple Parallel Interfaces
topics.description: Wave propagation through multiple planar boundaries, Fabry-Perot instruments, evanescent wave tunneling, and multilayer optical coatings.

key_concepts.name: Fabry-Perot Instrument
key_concepts.description: Optical resonator using multiple reflections between parallel surfaces to distinguish closely spaced wavelengths.

key_concepts.name: Multilayer Coatings
key_concepts.description: Systems of multiple thin-film dielectric layers engineered to control transmission and reflection spectra.

topics.name: Propagation in Anisotropic Media
topics.description: Constitutive relations and wave propagation in anisotropic crystals, including uniaxial and biaxial media.
subtopics: Refraction at a Uniaxial Crystal Surface
Poynting Vector in a Uniaxial Crystal

key_concepts.name: Uniaxial and Biaxial Crystals
key_concepts.description: Anisotropic optical media characterized by direction-dependent indices of refraction.

topics.name: Superposition of Quasi-Parallel Plane Waves
topics.description: Interference, frequency spectrum, group and phase velocity, wave packet propagation, and quadratic dispersion.
subtopics: Wave Packet Propagation and Group Delay

key_concepts.name: Group vs. Phase Velocity
key_concepts.description: Distinction between the velocity of individual wave phase fronts and the propagation speed of the overall wave packet envelope.

key_concepts.name: Quadratic Dispersion
key_concepts.description: Frequency-dependent phase distortion causing broadening or chirping of optical wave packets.

topics.name: Coherence Theory
topics.description: Temporal and spatial coherence of light, interferometry, fringe visibility, and Fourier spectroscopy.
subtopics: Young's Two-Slit Setup and Spatial Coherence

key_concepts.name: Michelson Interferometer
key_concepts.description: Two-beam interferometer used to measure optical path differences, coherence time, and spectral properties.

key_concepts.name: Coherence Time and Fringe Visibility
key_concepts.description: Measures of correlation in light fields determining the contrast of interference fringes over time or path delays.

topics.name: Light as Rays
topics.description: Geometrical optics approximations, the Eikonal equation, Fermat's principle, and ABCD matrix methods for paraxial optical systems.
subtopics: Reflection and Refraction at Curved Surfaces

key_concepts.name: Fermat's Principle
key_concepts.description: Principle stating that light rays follow paths of stationary optical transit time between two points.

key_concepts.name: Paraxial Rays and ABCD Matrices
key_concepts.description: Matrix formulation to trace ray position and slope through paraxial optical elements and interfaces.

topics.name: Diffraction Applications
topics.description: Applications of wave diffraction, including Fraunhofer diffraction with lenses, resolution limits, grating spectrometers, and Gaussian laser beams.

key_concepts.name: Diffraction Grating
key_concepts.description: Periodic optical element used to disperse light into constituent wavelengths via multi-slit interference and diffraction.

key_concepts.name: Gaussian Laser Beams
key_concepts.description: Diffraction and propagation characteristics of laser beams with Gaussian transverse field profiles.

topics.name: Interferograms and Holography
topics.description: Surface testing via optical interferograms and principles of holographic wavefront recording and reconstruction.

key_concepts.name: Holographic Wavefront Reconstruction
key_concepts.description: Recording and reconstructing the phase and amplitude of optical wavefronts to recreate three-dimensional fields.

topics.name: Blackbody Radiation
topics.description: Thermal radiation physics, thermodynamic derivation, Planck's formula, and Einstein's A and B transition coefficients.

key_concepts.name: Stefan-Boltzmann Law
key_concepts.description: Law relating the total radiant energy emitted by a blackbody to the fourth power of its absolute temperature.

key_concepts.name: Planck's Formula
key_concepts.description: Radiation formula resolving the failure of classical equipartition by quantizing energy states of radiation modes.
